article.title: Magnitude 6.2 earthquake shakes part of northern Japan

candidates.rawAssertion: A magnitude 6.2 earthquake shook part of northern Japan early Monday.
There was no damage or casualties reported from the earthquake in northern Japan.
No tsunami advisory was issued by the Japan Meteorological Agency following the earthquake.
The earthquake struck 18 kilometers (11 miles) west of the small town of Sarabetsu on Hokkaido.
The earthquake occurred at a depth of 81 kilometers (50 miles).
The U.S. Geological Survey measured the quake’s strength at 6.1 magnitude.
A week prior to the earthquake, a 7.7 magnitude offshore earthquake prompted an advisory for a possible megaquake.
Japan issued an advisory of a slightly higher risk of a possible megaquake for the northeastern coastal areas.
The Japan Meteorological Agency stated that Monday’s quake was outside of the area subject to a megaquake advisory.
The special awareness week regarding megaquakes is set to end as planned according to the JMA.
